\par\vspace{3pt}
{\footnotesize\raggedright Large-change months defined ex ante, i.e. known at $t-1$, with thresholds computed from the history up to the forecast origin (December of $Y-1$), as the article's shock masks. A: $|y_{t-12} - y_{t-1}|/y_{t-1}$ above its P75. B: $|\hat{y}_t - y_{t-1}|/y_{t-1}$ above its P75, with $\hat{y}_t$ the one-step forecast of the frozen SARIMA of the window. MAE/MASE at P75; Consistently = first or tied in at least 3 of P50, P60, P75 and P90 (rule of the article). C (not ex ante): months inside an El Ni\~no costero event of the official list of the Instituto Geof\'isico del Per\'u (IGP), based on the Coastal El Ni\~no Index (ICEN), a centred 3-month running mean of sea-surface temperature anomalies in the Ni\~no 1+2 region (ENFEN 2024 operational definition); events are declared after the fact, so C describes a contemporaneous state, not an ex-ante warning. ENFEN alert statements, which may declare events without the ICEN conditions, were not used. Events overlapping the test windows 2021--2025: 2023-03 to 2024-02. Rank in C: * = first or tied with the first (the 95\% bootstrap CI of the difference with the best model contains 0). $^{\dagger}$ Added after the protocol. MAE in tonnes; 95\% CI: paired bootstrap of months within each test window (B = 10,000, seed 42). All results in this table are post-protocol analyses (second review round) and do not modify the pre-registered ten-model ranking.\par}
